definitions.explanation: A formal religious ceremony or festival, typically associated with Shinto shrines or Buddhist temples. More formal and solemn in tone than the everyday word 祭り.

examples.japanese: ⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{祭礼|さいれい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{行|おこな}われた→行う：01238_okonau⟧。
examples.english: A religious ceremony was held at the shrine.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧{祭礼|さいれい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{毎年|まいとし}→毎年：00731_maitoshi⟧⟦{秋|あき}→秋：02276_aki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{開催|かいさい}される→開催する：10441_kaisaisuru⟧。
examples.english: This festival is held every autumn.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古|ふる}く→古い：00488_furui⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{伝|つた}わる→伝わる：01961_tsutawaru⟧{祭礼|さいれい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{地域|ちいき}→地域：01461_chiiki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人々|ひとびと}→人々：03141_hitobito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大勢|おおぜい}→大勢：02850_oozei⟧⟦{参加|さんか}する→参加する：25408_sankasuru⟧。
examples.english: Many local people participate in the traditional festival that has been passed down for generations.

notes:
Compound of {祭|さい} (festival, worship) and ⟦{礼|れい}→礼：02170_rei⟧ (ceremony, rite). A formal term that emphasizes the religious and ceremonial aspects of a festival, as opposed to the celebratory or entertainment aspects.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{祭|まつ}り→祭り：03735_matsuri⟧ — festival; the everyday, broad term covering both religious and secular events
- ⟦{儀式|ぎしき}→儀式：00071_gishiki⟧ — ceremony; ritual; more general, not limited to festivals
- ⟦{神事|しんじ}→神事：14066_shinji⟧ — Shinto ritual; specifically religious, not the public celebration
- {例祭|れいさい} — regular festival; the main annual festival of a shrine

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {祭礼|さいれい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{行|おこな}う→行う：01238_okonau⟧ — to hold a religious festival
- {祭礼|さいれい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{参加|さんか}する→参加する：25408_sankasuru⟧ — to participate in a festival
- ⟦{伝統的|でんとうてき}→伝統的：04802_dentouteki⟧な{祭礼|さいれい} — traditional religious festival
- ⟦{秋|あき}→秋：02276_aki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{祭礼|さいれい} — autumn festival

REGISTER:
Formal and written. In everyday conversation, ⟦{祭|まつ}り→祭り：03735_matsuri⟧ or ⟦お{祭|まつ}り→お祭り：01349_omatsuri⟧ is much more common.
